messages:
maya: Heads up — started seeing a spike in GPU pod evictions in ap-se1 around 09:24 UTC. Evictions look tied to volume attach/detach timeouts, not OOMs. Anyone else seeing attach latency?

ashwin: Confirmed. Alert history shows attach failures for volumes backing /dev/nvme* on nodes gpu-rack-3a-*.

liam: What do the kubelet logs show on one of the nodes?

ashwin: Pasted a short tail from attach-detach-controller logs:

```
E0908 09:23:45.123456 1 reconciler.go:374] AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-6a3f" : rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
I0908 09:23:47.987654 1 operation_executor.go:826] AttachVolume.Attach succeeded for volume "pvc-6a3f" after 2m2s
```

julia: So some attaches are taking >2 minutes. Scheduler is binding, pod goes InitContainer->waiting, then kubelet times out and we trigger eviction back to queue. That churn is causing binpack oscillation and fragmentation in the GPU pools.

maya: We also saw netflap around the same time (router logs show transient disconnects for the AZ). Could be that CSI attach RPCs are getting delayed and retries push attach time way up.

liam: Node kernel logs (dmesg) from gpu-rack-3a-node-07 show repeated nvme reset lines and a couple PCIe link retrain messages. Might be hardware flakiness compounding the network issue.

ashwin: Quick grep from a problematic node: `journalctl -u kubelet | grep "AttachVolume" | tail -n 10` shows a chain of AttachVolume timeouts followed by eventual success. 

julia: Two action items: 1) short-term mitigation: reduce churn by preventing new high-priority training jobs from landing in ap-se1 and route to us-west2. 2) ops to rotate the three most noisy nodes in the r3 rack as a canary.

maya: Agreed. Also thinking about scheduler tweak: increase the attach timeout window before the scheduler marks pod as failed-to-start. Might stop the immediate eviction loop while we identify root cause.

liam: We can set a cluster-level heuristic for GPU node groups to use a longer BindTimeout for volumes. But that's risky — could hide real attach failures. Maybe do it only for a Canary node pool.

ashwin: Filed INF-2179 with logs and node names. Plan: cordon + drain two nodes in ap-se1-canary, monitor eviction rate for 15m, then decide whether to roll the rest.

julia: Short-term scheduler knob: bump kube-scheduler `pressure-transition-period`? Or we can patch our custom prebind check to wait on CSI attach result before finalizing binding. That is safer.

maya: @sre-bot what's the current eviction rate and GPU pool fragmentation metric?

sre-bot: ALERT: eviction-rate.ap-se1.gpu > 6/min in the last 5m. Fragmentation index for gpu-pool-ap-se1 increased from 0.22 -> 0.46 in last 30m.

maya: Ok start the canary rotate now. I'll also open a temporary placement policy to route new job submissions away from ap-se1.

liam: I'll watch hardware telemetry and file vendor ticket if NVMe errors persist.

ashwin: Workaround commands for operators if they need to inspect:

```bash
# check recent attach failures
journalctl -u kubelet --since "20 minutes ago" | grep AttachVolume | tail -n 50
# show pods that were evicted due to attach timeout
kubectl get events --field-selector reason=FailedAttachVolume -n ml --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 40
```

julia: Post-mortem followups: add a scheduler prebind wait on CSI attach for GPU pools, add a synthetic healthcheck for NVMe and PCIe errors to auto-drain nodes, and add a routing fallback to remote regions when attach latency trends up.

maya: Thanks — rolling now. Ping in 20m with status. :thumbsup:
